DORSET DIVISION / LEGAL

Terms of Service

Last updated: 25 October 2026

Who you are working with

Dorset Division is the trading name of Marnie Danson, a sole trader based in Poole, Dorset, United Kingdom. These terms cover services agreed directly with Dorset Division. The contracting business and its address are identified in Legal Information.

Email marnie@dorsetdivision.co.uk or telephone 07342 729158. Postal contact details are in Legal Information. Services are remote; there is no public walk-in office.

Agreeing a project

An enquiry, conversation with Burt or call booking does not by itself create a paid project. Before work starts, the written quote or proposal will identify the services, deliverables, price, payment schedule, intended timetable, revision allowance and any exclusions. Please check it and ask about anything unclear. Work starts after written acceptance and receipt of any agreed initial payment, subject to consumer cancellation rights. Contracts are agreed in English, and you will receive a copy of the agreed terms and scope in a form you can keep.

Scope, changes and client input

Please provide accurate instructions, materials you have permission to use, appropriate access and timely decisions. Use a secure access method rather than sending passwords in website forms or chat. Changes to the brief, deliverables, deadlines or revision allowance must be agreed in writing, including any extra price or time, before additional work is undertaken. Delayed materials or approvals may affect the timetable; I will explain any proposed changes.

Delivery and revisions

I will provide services with reasonable care and skill. Milestones, formats, review periods and included revisions are set out in the project agreement. Please report problems promptly so I can investigate. A review deadline does not remove your statutory rights. Any ongoing maintenance, hosting, training or support must be included in the agreed scope or arranged separately.

Prices, payments and third-party costs

Prices are in pounds sterling unless the quote says otherwise. Dorset Division is not registered for VAT and does not charge VAT. The total payable, payment dates and any separately payable costs will be confirmed before you accept. Website starting prices apply to defined work and are not an automatic quote for every project. Paid apps, hosting, domains, advertising, printing, licences and other outside costs require prior agreement. See Deposits & Payments.

Ownership and licences

Your quote will explain which final deliverables and rights you receive. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, rights to agreed final deliverables transfer only after the relevant invoices are paid, to the extent I am entitled to transfer them. Third-party artwork, fonts, software, stock assets and platform components remain subject to their licences. Rejected concepts, working files, reusable tools and pre-existing materials are not automatically transferred. Any continuing licence needed to use a final deliverable will be explained.

Confidentiality and personal information

Non-public project information is treated confidentially, except where disclosure is authorised, necessary to deliver the agreed service using appropriate providers, or required by law. Client access is used only for agreed work. Where I process personal data on your behalf, suitable written data-processing terms and security arrangements must be agreed before that processing begins. See the Privacy Policy.

Third-party platforms and professional boundaries

Marketplaces, hosting providers, publishers, payment providers and advertising platforms control their own services, rules, fees and approvals. I cannot guarantee rankings, sales, registrations, platform approvals or commercial outcomes. Business research and practical recommendations are not regulated legal, tax, investment or medical advice. Specialist advice may be needed for a particular decision. Burt provides general assistance and cannot agree prices, contracts, refunds or deadlines.

Responsibility and legal rights

Each party remains responsible for its own acts and omissions. Nothing excludes or limits liability for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, death or personal injury caused by negligence, or any liability that cannot lawfully be excluded. Consumer rights, including rights to services provided with reasonable care and skill, remain unaffected. Any additional project-specific liability arrangement must be expressly agreed, fair and lawful.

Ending work and resolving concerns

If you need to cancel or pause work, contact me promptly. The agreed terms, work delivered, reasonable unavoidable costs and applicable law determine what is payable or refundable; a deposit is not automatically forfeited. See Cancellations & Refunds and Accessibility & Complaints. If I cannot complete the work, I will explain the position and account fairly for undelivered services.

Governing law and changes

Direct project agreements are governed by the laws of England and Wales, subject to mandatory protections that apply to consumers in their country of residence. Nothing prevents a consumer from using a court available to them under applicable law. Updating this website does not retrospectively change an existing agreement; changes to an agreed project require written agreement. Work booked through PeoplePerHour or another marketplace also remains subject to that platform’s applicable terms and payment rules.
